cards.text: Saul is dead, and now there are TWO kings. The men of Judah anointed David king in Hebron, and Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over Israel (2 Samuel 2:4, 8-9). One day Abner and the servants of Ish-bosheth march out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

cards.question: Abner's side is headed for Gibeon. Who marches out with David's servants to meet them?

cards.text: Two groups, one pool of Gibeon, each side lined up across the water from the other. It's a four-way stop where NOBODY wants to go first, until Abner finally speaks up to Joab.

cards.question: Abner looks across the pool at Joab and makes a suggestion. What is it?

answers.text: Let the young men compete before them
Let the two kings meet and talk
Let both sides go home in peace

cards.question: Joab turns down Abner's idea.
The young men at the pool of Gibeon get up and are counted off, ___ on each side.

cards.text: Twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth. Twelve for David. They step up face to face, and the whole pool goes quiet.

cards.question: When the twenty-four young men at Gibeon go at each other, one side clearly wins the contest.

cards.text: Each man grabs his opponent by the head and thrusts his sword into his side, and they all fall together. That place in Gibeon gets a name: Helkath-hazzurim.

cards.question: After the contest at the pool, the battle that day is intense. Who ends up defeated?

answers.text: Abner and the men of Israel
Joab and the servants of David
The Philistines who join the fight

cards.text: The three sons of Zeruiah are there: Joab, Abishai and Asahel, and Asahel is fleet of foot like a wild gazelle. Me? I'm on a gold base, friend. My top speed is HOP.

cards.question: In the middle of the battle, speedy Asahel takes off running after ___.
Asahel chases Abner without turning to the right or to the left.

cards.text: Abner glances back: “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel says it is, and I LOVE this, the man is getting chased across a battlefield and he STILL checks caller ID.

cards.question: Abner tells Asahel to turn to his right or his left. What does he tell him to do instead of chasing him?

answers.text: Grab one of the young men and take his gear
Go back and wait with his brother Joab
Drop his weapons and head home to Hebron

cards.question: Asahel takes Abner's advice and stops chasing him.

cards.text: So Abner warns him a second time: “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground?”

cards.question: Abner adds one more question to his warning. Who does he say he couldn't show his face to if he struck Asahel down?
Asahel still refuses to turn away from Abner. What happens?

answers.text: Abner strikes him with the butt of his spear
Asahel catches Abner and takes his spear
Joab runs up and calls Asahel off the chase

cards.text: Asahel falls dead on the spot. And “every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.”
Asahel is gone, but his brothers Joab and Abishai keep after Abner. By sunset they've come as far as the hill of Ammah, on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

cards.question: Joab and Abishai are closing in on Abner at sunset. What do the Benjamites with Abner do?

answers.text: Rally to Abner and take a stand on a hill
Scatter and run home to Mahanaim
Hand Abner over to Joab and Abishai

cards.text: Then Abner calls down from the hill to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness?”

cards.question: Abner asks Joab how long it'll be before he does something. What does Abner want Joab to do?

answers.text: Tell the troops to stop chasing their brothers
Meet him alone on top of the hill
Bring King David out to talk with him

cards.question: Joab answers Abner that if he hadn't spoken up, the troops would have kept pursuing their brothers until ___.
Joab blows the ram's horn, and his troops charge up the hill after Abner.

cards.text: All the troops stop, and the fighting is over. Then all that night Abner and his men march through the Arabah and cross the Jordan.

cards.question: After marching all morning, Abner and his men arrive back at ___.
Joab comes back from chasing Abner and gathers all his troops. How do the two sides' losses compare?

answers.text: David's side lost far fewer men
Both sides lost about the same
Abner's side lost far fewer men

cards.text: Besides Asahel, nineteen of David's servants are missing. But they struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.

cards.question: David's men take Asahel and bury him in his father's tomb in ___.

cards.text: Then Joab and his men march all night and reach Hebron at daybreak. Two armies, two all-nighters, and the last all-nighter I pulled was counting dust in the back of that junk drawer, and I LOST COUNT.

cards.question: After Gibeon, the war between the house of Saul and the house of David ends quickly.
The war between Saul's house and David's house drags on. What happens to the two sides over time?

answers.text: David grows stronger and Saul's house grows weaker
Saul's house grows stronger and David grows weaker
Both sides keep growing weaker and weaker

cards.text: Back in Hebron, six sons are born to David, each by a different mother, including his firstborn Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel, and his third son Absalom, son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur. Two houses, one long war, and trust me, friend, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: "Saul is dead" is a Bible fact from outside the passage, and it has no reference. The other outside facts on the card do carry one (2 Samuel 2:4, 8-9).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card uses facts from 2 Samuel 2:4 and 2:8-9, which come before the passage. It cites them inline, but its verses field gives only 2 Samuel 2:12. The citation rule says first verse used to last, which would mean 2:4-12. That range reaches outside the passage.
findings.question: When an opening card uses outside facts with an inline reference, should its verses field cite only the passage verses it tells, or every verse it uses, including verses outside the passage?

findings.problem: "until Abner finally speaks up" tells a standoff and a delay as story fact. The text only says the two groups took positions and then Abner spoke (2 Samuel 2:13-14). Nothing in it says anyone waited or held back. The four-way stop joke is fine as a joke, but the narration line adds a time and a situation the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card mostly repeats the answer to card 6 (twelve on each side, 2 Samuel 2:15). It adds only scene-setting, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

The card asks whether one side clearly wins the contest before the baker has been told anything about how it goes. Card 7 only says the men step up face to face. Nothing points toward "they all fell together" (2 Samuel 2:16), and the true answer goes against what a contest would lead anyone to expect. Getting it right is luck. Card 9 tells the outcome afterward, so the question could be moved after a setup or replaced.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Right after "Asahel says it is," the joke's "the man is getting chased" and "he STILL checks caller ID" can read as Asahel, who is the one chasing. The reader has to work out that it means Abner. The second sentence also packs Asahel's reply, an aside and the punchline into one comma-spliced line.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Joab's wording ("until morning" against "midnight" or "noon") in a line they haven't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason it out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Two houses, one long war" restates 2 Samuel 3:1, but the card cites only 2 Samuel 3:2-5.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
